# Provenance — tests/sample_data

**All files here are SYNTHETIC.** They were procedurally generated by
`generate_sample_data.py` (committed in this directory) and contain no frames,
audio, or metadata from any real space, phone, or person. Every rendered frame
carries a burned-in **SYNTHETIC** watermark so the data can never be mistaken
for a real capture.

## How each file was made

| File | Generator step | Tooling |
|---|---|---|
| `images/sample_synthetic_01..08.jpg` | A one-point-perspective corridor is drawn per frame in pure Python (RGB integer math; the camera slides laterally across the 8 frames), written as PPM, then encoded to baseline JPEG (`-q:v 5`) with ffmpeg's `+bitexact`/`-map_metadata -1` flags so the output is byte-deterministic per ffmpeg build. | python3 stdlib + ffmpeg (libjpeg via ffmpeg) |
| `synthetic_capture_bundle.zip` | The same 8 JPEG bytes are packed into a studio **prepared-capture** export: `manifest.json` at the archive root (schemaVersion 1, bundleKind `prepared-capture`, 1 room, 2 view groups, per-image sha256/bytes/width/height/stagedAt) plus `images/<sha256>.jpg` members. This is byte-contract-compatible with `apps/studio/src/lib/capture/exportBundle.ts` (the zod schema in `apps/studio/src/types/scene.ts`) and is parsed by `apps/studio/scripts/prepare_capture.py`. ZIP member timestamps are fixed (2026-01-01) for determinism. | python3 stdlib `zipfile` |
| `synthetic_clip.mp4` | 20 drawn corridor frames (lateral camera slide) are encoded as a 5 s @ 4 fps H.264 (`libx264`, `yuv420p`) clip with bitexact/metadata-stripping flags. | python3 stdlib + ffmpeg (libx264) |

Regeneration is byte-for-byte deterministic for a given ffmpeg build:

```bash
python3 tests/sample_data/generate_sample_data.py
```

The digests inside `synthetic_capture_bundle.zip`'s `manifest.json` are exactly
the per-image digests above (the ZIP stores the same bytes), so
`prepare_capture.py` verifies them offline without trusting the manifest.

## Licensing and rights

- These files contain **zero third-party content** — no stock photos, no
  recorded video, no personally identifiable data. They are 100% machine-drawn
  pixels from the committed generator script.
- They are released under the same terms as this repository (the project's own
  license; if the repository root has no `LICENSE` file yet, treat this
  directory as all-rights-reserved project material — reuse requires the
  project owner's permission).
- ffmpeg/libx264 encode the pixels but contribute no content; the encoded
  files contain no ffmpeg metadata (stripped via `-map_metadata -1` and
  `+bitexact`).
- **Not for accuracy claims:** synthetic frames are ideal, texture-rich input.
  Passing ingestion on them says nothing about how the pipeline behaves on a
  real handheld capture (see the root README's honest BLK-001 limitation).
